sun.upright:
An Aries Sun usually knows what it wants before the question's finished, so the Seven of Cups is an awkward card to be handed. Seven offers floating in a cloud and, for once, nothing obvious to grab first. The card is Venus in Scorpio, and Venus is in detriment there. It's in detriment in your sign as well. So the planet of desire is uncomfortable on both sides of this pairing, which goes some way to explaining why wanting things feels unusually complicated for you.

Aries and Scorpio share an old ruler in Mars, but they sit five signs apart, a quincunx, an angle with nothing in common that needs small adjustments all the time. Add fire meeting water and you get steam. Plenty of heat and wanting, and not much forward motion. From the inside it feels like your decisiveness has gone missing. You pick a direction on Monday, a different one looks better by Wednesday, and you're cross with yourself about it. I've seen a lot of Aries Suns read this as losing their nerve. Usually the thing you want this time just can't be won by getting there first.

At work it tends to look like three new plans in a fortnight, each one exciting for about four days. With money, it's buying the gear for a hobby before you've tried the hobby. In a couple, you might want the other person to choose for you and then resent it when they do. If you were born in the last ten degrees of Aries, Venus rules that decan, the Four of Wands, so this is less foreign than it feels. Give yourself a short deadline and pick one plan by it.
sun.reversed:
Standing in front of seven choices is torture for an Aries Sun, and with the card reversed the usual fix is to grab the brightest one just to end the discomfort. The decision gets made fast and loud, and it's made for the version of you in your head, the one who's already won. Venus is out of its depth in Aries and in Scorpio alike, so what you want and what you'd actually enjoy can end up quite far apart.

It shows in the job you quit on a Friday for a plan that was mostly a feeling, or the course you signed up for because of the photos on the website. Romantically, you might fall hard for someone's potential and ignore the actual person. Before you commit to the next big thing, tell one blunt friend the whole plan and let them ask the boring questions.

moon.upright:
Anger gets said, boredom gets a walk, a crush gets a text. An Aries Moon feels something and does something about it in the same breath, and the Seven of Cups slows that loop down in a way you probably won't enjoy. It's a water card and your Moon is fire, and those two elements are opposed, so feelings that usually flare up and burn off get soaked instead, and they hang around.

Venus is in detriment in both Aries and Scorpio, which leaves the planet of pleasure and comfort awkward on each side of this. What normally soothes you, the run, the quick fix, starting something new, doesn't settle you the usual way, and your mind fills the gap with pictures. The flat you could move to, the person you could call, the life you'd have if you just left. Aries Moons aren't natural daydreamers, since it feels too passive, so it comes out as restlessness. A jiggling leg. Lying awake with three plans going at once. The quincunx between the two signs keeps you making small corrections all day without ever quite getting comfortable.

Late at night it can look like scrolling rental listings or old messages at one in the morning. In the body it's energy with nowhere to go, so hard exercise helps more than usual. With a partner you might pick a fight, because a fight at least feels like something happening. Before bed, write down the three daydreams that keep coming back and cross out the one you'd never actually do.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, the card can turn an Aries Moon's cravings into quick exits. Something upsets you and within the hour you've booked something, bought something, messaged someone you shouldn't have. Each one is a small escape into a better picture, and none of them touch what's actually bothering you. Mars rules Aries, and traditionally it rules Scorpio as well, so there's real anger under the wanting, and it's being fed sweets when it needs to be heard.

The bank statement usually shows it first, along with the gap between how good an idea felt at midnight and how it looks the next day. Friends may notice you swinging between big plans and flatness. When the urge to get out hits, go for a hard walk first and see what the feeling is once your body's tired.

rising.upright:
Aries rising walks into a room like it's already decided something. With the Seven of Cups on it, strangers may meet a slightly different person, someone who seems up for anything and hard to pin down. Your chart ruler is Mars, and Mars is also the old ruler of Scorpio, the card's sign, so there's a thread between you and this card even though the two signs sit a quincunx apart with little to say to each other.

What happens is that your instinct to start things fast gets flooded with options. You say yes to the drinks, the side project, the weekend away, the new gym, because each one looks good in the moment and yes is always Aries rising's first move. Venus sits badly in Aries and just as badly in Scorpio, so charm doesn't come out in its usual tidy way. People may read you as flirting when you're only enthusiastic, or as keen on a plan you've barely thought about. Other people see their own wishes in you. Counting whole signs from Aries, Scorpio falls on your eighth house, so some of those wishes run deep, about money or closeness, and they arrive faster than you'd expect.

At work you might get volunteered for things because you look eager. In dating, someone could decide you're keener than you are. Your style may get more playful, a colour you wouldn't usually wear. Before you say yes to the next invitation, wait until the following morning to answer.
rising.reversed:
Enthusiastic starts pile up when Aries rising meets this card reversed. You pitch the idea in the meeting, sign up for the fun run, tell the new neighbour you'll have them over, and then the follow-through goes missing because the next shiny thing has arrived. Your fire and the card's water are opposed, and here the steam is mostly talk. People you've just met can end up with a picture of you that you can't live up to.

New workplaces are where it costs you most, since first impressions stick and a name for big ideas quickly becomes a name for not finishing them. It can sour a new friendship too, when the dinner you promised never happens. Keep a list of what you've offered people lately and do the smallest one first.

sun.upright:
Venus is your planet, Taurus, and in this card it's about as far from home as it can get. Scorpio is your opposite sign, and Venus in Scorpio is in detriment, which is astrology's way of saying it's living in somebody else's house and nothing's where it expects. So when the Seven of Cups turns up for a Taurus Sun, it's your own ruler, the planet that knows exactly what you like, arriving a bit dazzled by choice.

That's unusual for you. Taurus Suns tend to want a few good things, reliably, and aren't easily fooled by shine. The opposition pulls you toward Scorpio's end of the axis, where wanting is deep and secretive and a bit obsessive, and it can have you fantasising about a life nothing like the steady one you've built. Another city, another career, a bigger house, somebody who isn't your partner. Earth and water do suit each other, so these daydreams aren't wasted, and a couple of them might be the start of something that grows. The difficulty is that both ends of this axis are fixed signs, and neither likes letting go of an option once it's been imagined.

With money, watch the pull toward one big purchase that stands for a whole new life, the car, the renovation, the expensive course. At work, a job offer could look better on paper than in person, so go and see the place. In the body you might want more comfort food and more sleep, and some of that's fine. Price the daydream properly, in money and in hours, before you decide how you feel about it.
sun.reversed:
Taurus Suns can dig in on a dream the same way they dig in on everything else, and that's the usual shape of this card reversed. You chose a cup a while ago, the business, the house, the person, and you've kept polishing it even though what's inside has turned out thinner than you hoped. Venus rules your sign and struggles in Scorpio, so your normally sharp sense of value can get its sums wrong.

Money is where it bites, putting more in because of what's already gone in. A relationship can get the same treatment, loyalty to how it was supposed to turn out. At work it's the role you took for the title. Sit down with one plan you've been defending and list what it's actually given you in the last year, in plain terms.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon settles through the body. A good meal, clean sheets, the same walk at the same hour, someone's hand on your back. Venus rules Taurus, so when this card arrives with Venus in it, it's your own comfort planet turning up, only it's come from Scorpio, the sign opposite yours, where it's restless and in detriment. The easy pleasures that usually work might feel slightly off.

What tends to happen is that craving gets bigger and vaguer. You want something and can't say what, so you try the obvious things. Another biscuit, another episode, another look at the holiday house you'll never book. Scorpio's end of the axis wants intensity and privacy, your Moon wants calm and routine, and the opposition puts you in the middle of that pull. The elements help, since water and earth get along. Under all the grazing there's usually one real longing, often for more closeness with someone or for time that's genuinely yours, and you can find it if you slow down.

Food is the first place to look, eating to fill a gap that isn't hunger. In a relationship you may be imagining a different kind of intimacy and not saying so. Sleep may be heavy and full of dreams. Next time you reach for something to soothe yourself, stop and say out loud what you'd have if you could have anything.
moon.reversed:
Routine is how a Taurus Moon protects itself, and when this card turns over the routine can become a hiding place. You stop letting yourself want anything new, because wanting feels risky, so you eat the same things, watch the same shows and call it contentment. The pull from Scorpio across the axis doesn't stop, though, and the longing leaks out sideways as moodiness or a sudden expensive treat.

At home it shows up as clutter, things bought for comfort and never used. Between you and a partner there may be a flat patch you've both agreed not to mention. Your body might feel sluggish, slow to get going in the mornings. Change one small thing in your week, a different route, a new dish, and notice how much you resist it.

rising.upright:
With Taurus rising, Venus is your chart ruler, and Scorpio is the sign on your seventh house, the one facing you across the table. The Seven of Cups is Venus in Scorpio. So this card puts your own ruler over on the partners' side of the chart, in detriment, and that says a lot about how you're meeting people.

Normally you come across as calm and unhurried, someone comfortable in their own skin. With this card, people might find you alluring in a way that's harder to read, and they'll project onto that. The client thinks you're about to sign. The date thinks you've fallen for them. You haven't decided anything. Earth and water are on good terms and both signs are fixed, so the impression lasts, which is lovely when it's accurate and awkward when it isn't. From your side, the instinct is to take your time before starting anything, and with seven possible openings that can take a very long time indeed.

In business, be clear in writing about what you've agreed to. In your style there may be a pull toward something richer and darker, velvet, deep colours, and it's worth indulging. With someone new, notice whether you like them or the idea of them. Say plainly what you want early in a first meeting, even if it feels abrupt to you.
rising.reversed:
Taurus rising with the Seven of Cups reversed can look lovely and give nothing away. People take your calm as agreement, and you let them, because correcting them would mean deciding. Your chart ruler is in detriment in the card's sign, and the result can be a pleasant manner sitting on top of real indecision.

At work it shows when someone assumes you're on board and you quietly aren't. In dating it can be keeping two people interested because choosing feels too final. It can also look like never starting the thing you keep describing to friends, the shop, the garden, the move. Find one person who's been waiting on an answer from you and give it to them, yes or no.

sun.upright:
Seven options is a normal Tuesday for a Gemini Sun. You're good at holding lots of things at once, and you'd usually enjoy a card like this, all those cups and possibilities. The difference is that this is a water card, Venus in Scorpio, and these aren't ideas you're juggling. They're wants, and they come with feelings attached, which is a different kind of weight to carry around.

Scorpio and Gemini are five signs apart, a quincunx, an angle with no common ground that asks for constant small corrections. Air and water don't clash and don't click either, so they have to be introduced. Venus has no special standing in Gemini and picks up Mercury's habits, which means desire tends to come through your head first, as a plan or a conversation or a tab left open. The tension is that you can talk yourself into or out of anything, and this card is about the wants that don't respond to talk. You may notice you've argued well for five different futures and still feel unsettled, because the real preference is lower down and quieter.

At work it's the job ads saved, the side business sketched in your notes app, the course you've half enrolled in. With friends it can be making plans with three different groups for the same weekend. With a sibling there might be an old rivalry about who got to be what. Stop explaining the options to other people for a while, and just notice which one you keep thinking about when you're not talking.
sun.reversed:
The trap for a Gemini Sun with this card turned over is keeping every option alive by talking about it. As long as it's still being discussed, nothing's been lost. So the career change stays a good story, the move interstate stays a maybe, and you're known as someone with interesting plans. Mercury colours Venus in your sign, and here it's turning desire into chat.

Friends usually notice before you do, around the time they stop asking how the plan's going. At work you can be spread over too many things to do any of them well. It can also make you restless in love, bored as soon as something's settled. Choose one plan you've talked about for over a year and either start it properly or stop mentioning it.

moon.upright:
Gemini Moons calm down by talking. You work out how you feel by saying it to someone, or texting it, or reading about it until it makes sense. The Seven of Cups brings a kind of feeling that doesn't sort easily into words. Longings, half-formed pictures, the sense of wanting something you can't name. It's a water card meeting an air Moon, two elements that have never really been introduced.

The quincunx between Scorpio and Gemini adds to the awkwardness, five signs apart and nothing much shared, so you keep having to adjust. Venus is a guest in Gemini with no dignity to speak of, taking on Mercury's colouring, and you'll probably try to think your way through what you feel. Research, lists, asking everyone's opinion. It helps a bit. Then at two in the morning you're back where you started, imagining a different life in some detail and slightly embarrassed by how much you want it. That's fine. Gemini Moons are allowed feelings that don't make sense yet.

Your phone is often where it shows, lots of messages started and not sent. With a sibling or a close friend, you might confide something you didn't plan to. Sleep can be busy with dreams you remember in pieces. Try describing the daydream to one person without explaining why you want it.
moon.reversed:
Twenty tabs open, three podcasts started, messages out to five people, and none of it lands. A Gemini Moon with this card reversed can keep a feeling at arm's length by never staying on it long enough to feel it. You change the subject, including inside your own head. Air and water haven't been introduced here, and the feeling is being kept out of the conversation on purpose.

Evenings are where it shows, the restless scrolling, the snacking, a vague dread you can't account for. With a partner it can be chatting about everything except the one thing that matters. Your nerves might feel frayed by the end of the week. Put the phone in another room for an hour and let whatever you've been dodging turn up.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising makes a quick first impression, bright, chatty, interested in everyone. The Seven of Cups gives it a dreamier edge, and strangers might see you as someone with a lot going on, several stories, several possible directions. They'll each pick a different one to believe.

Mercury rules your chart, and Venus only borrows Mercury's ways in Gemini, so the card's charm comes through how you talk. You'll be good at describing possibilities, and people will buy them. Scorpio is five signs on from Gemini, a quincunx, and counting whole signs it falls on your sixth house, the daily job and the routine. That's where the card's longing tends to collect. You meet the world sparkly and open, and then the ordinary working week feels thin beside it, so the daydreams start there, at the desk or on the commute. It's a small mismatch and it keeps nagging.

At work you may pitch well and then find the task itself dull. In your look it might mean trying on different styles, a new haircut every couple of months. Socially you'll meet a lot of people and come home feeling you haven't really met anyone. Pick one new acquaintance and have a second, longer conversation with them.
rising.reversed:
Put Gemini rising together with this card reversed and you get someone who says yes to everything at the door. You'll come, you'll help, you'd love to, and people walk away with a picture of you that you haven't agreed to. Mercury's quickness and Venus's wish to please make a slippery mix, and the quincunx means you're forever adjusting to whoever's in front of you.

At work it's promising deadlines to keep a meeting pleasant. With new friends it's the plan made on a night out that never happens. It can leave you feeling vaguely guilty in lots of directions at once. Before agreeing to something, say you'll check and get back to them, and then actually get back to them.

sun.upright:
Look at the cups floating in the cloud and find the one with a castle in it. For a Cancer Sun that's the cup to watch, because what you're usually building is a home, a family, somewhere people can come back to. The Seven of Cups is water and so are you, and Scorpio sits a trine from Cancer, four signs apart in the same element. The card flows straight in without much resistance.

Same-element pairings amplify, for better and for too much. You'll feel the card's longing as your own, and you'll probably feel it about home and the people in it. Should you move, have another child, bring a parent in to live with you, renovate, start again somewhere cheaper. Each option comes with a whole imagined life, and Cancer Suns can furnish an imagined life down to the tea towels. Venus is a visitor in Cancer, helped by nothing and hindered by nothing, and it moves with the Moon's tides, so the wanting comes in waves. Certain on Monday, gone by Thursday. If your birthday's in the first ten degrees of Cancer, that decan belongs to Venus, the Two of Cups, and the pull toward one particular person may be what's really behind all of it.

With family, you may be planning everyone's future a little too tenderly. With money, a property listing can become an evening's entertainment and then a week's mood. At work, the job that promises security might be getting a longer look than it deserves. Talk to the people you're picturing in these futures and find out what they're picturing.
sun.reversed:
With the card upside down, a Cancer Sun can build a perfect home in its head and hide in it. The family Christmas that goes exactly right, the partner who finally understands, the house by the water. Meanwhile the real house needs a conversation nobody's having. Water on water has nothing to slow it, so the fantasy can get very detailed.

With family it comes out as disappointment that people won't be who you'd planned. With a partner there can be sulking over a future they never agreed to. You might also be putting off a practical decision about money or where to live, because every option spoils the picture. Write down the one thing at home you'd change first if the picture weren't in the way.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon feels everything at full volume and remembers all of it. The Seven of Cups comes from Scorpio, another water sign, a trine away, and what it brings sits very comfortably in you. Longing, reverie, the sense of possibility that comes up late in the evening when the house is quiet. Nothing in the pairing slows it down, and you'll probably feel it most after dark.

Venus has no dignity in Cancer and goes along with the Moon, so what you want comes and goes with your moods. You might feel homesick for places you've never lived, or miss a version of your family that never quite existed. Old photos can set it off, or a smell, a song, a friend's holiday pictures. Cancer Moons tend to comfort themselves by imagining the safe, full house, and with this card that imagining can take up a good part of the day. Some of it's useful, because a longing tells you what you're short of. Some of it just goes round and round.

In the body it can show as broken sleep, or eating for comfort in the evenings. With your mother, or whoever mothered you, old feelings might come up, soft ones and sore ones. With a partner you may want more tenderness than you're asking for. Ask for one specific kind of care, a cup of tea brought to bed, a call on the way home, and notice how it feels to get it.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed can turn a Cancer Moon's softness into a sealed room. You retreat into memories and daydreams where everyone behaves as they should, and the real people around you get shut out without knowing why. The Moon rules both your sign and your moods, the card adds more water, and a feeling can swell until it's all you can see.

At home it looks like going quiet for days and expecting people to guess. Physically it can be sleeping too much or grazing late. With family, an old hurt may be replaying in a kinder version you've made up, one where they apologise properly. Tell the person you're hurt by what actually happened, in two sentences, and leave the imagined version out of it.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising usually meets people gently, a little guarded, warm once you've decided they're safe. The Seven of Cups adds something dreamy and romantic to that first impression, and you may find strangers approaching you with less hesitation, and imagining things about you with even less.

Scorpio is a trine from Cancer, same element, and it falls on your fifth house when you count whole signs, the house of romance, play and creative pleasure. Venus has its joy in the fifth, so the card's desire lands somewhere it likes. Your instinct is to start things the way you'd start a crush, slowly, with a lot of wondering. The Moon is your chart ruler. Venus is neither helped nor hindered in Cancer and follows the Moon's lead, so how you come across can change with your mood, open one day and shy the next. People will pick up on the softness and the fantasy in it. Someone may decide after one conversation that you're exactly what they've been looking for, which is flattering and a bit much.

In dating, you may attract people who like the idea of you. Creatively it's a good stretch for starting something small and playful without deciding what it's for. With colleagues your warmth will open doors, as long as you're clear about what you can take on. When someone new starts telling you who you are, ask them a question about themselves.
rising.reversed:
A daydream makes a good hiding place for Cancer rising when this card turns over. You come across as sweet and a bit far away, and people fill in the gaps with their own wishes, which suits you, because it means nobody gets too close. The trine lets the card's water flow in easily, and you use it to keep people at a distance.

In new relationships it can be letting someone fall for a version of you that you can't keep up. At work it's nodding along to a plan you privately doubt, and letting the team think you're fine with it. With a new friend you might mother them so you don't have to be known. Next time someone asks how you are, give them one true detail.

sun.upright:
The laurel wreath is the cup a Leo Sun tends to spot first. Recognition, the win, being the one people talk about on the drive home. This card carries Venus in Scorpio, and Scorpio squares Leo, three signs apart and both fixed, which is friction that won't let either side sit still for long. Venus has no rank in your sign and borrows the Sun's manners there, so what this card stirs up comes out warm and proud and wanting an audience.

Part of the trouble is that Scorpio likes to want things privately, and a Leo Sun likes to want them out loud. Fire and water are opposed elements, so a lot of this runs as steam. You picture the big version of your life, the stage, your name on the book, the house people would stop outside, and it's so vivid it feels half done. Then someone asks what you've actually started and it stings, because you're proud and you know the answer. With two fixed signs in the mix, letting any of the seven go can feel like letting yourself down.

At work it's the promotion you've already imagined announcing, with a bit of quiet resentment toward whoever's in the way. With a creative project it's the finished thing admired in your head while the first draft sits there. In love, you might want to be adored in one very particular way and never have said which. Pick the dream you'd still want if nobody ever saw you do it, and give it an hour of unglamorous work before the weekend's out.
sun.reversed:
A Leo Sun with this card upside down can start performing the dream in place of living it. You talk about the restaurant you'll open or the album that's nearly ready, people are impressed, and being impressed quietly does the job the dream was meant to do. The square to Scorpio pushes for action, and with the card turned over, the push all goes into the telling. Venus picks up the Sun's pride in your sign, so it hurts to admit a plan has stalled.

Friends will hear the same story for the third year running and stop asking. At work you might be guarding the title and letting the job under it slide. In love there can be a sulk when a partner doesn't admire the plan enough. Tell one person the plan has stalled and what stalled it, without dressing it up.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon needs to matter to somebody. Nothing grand, usually. Noticed, thanked, somebody's favourite at least once a day. The Seven of Cups comes in from Scorpio, which squares Leo, and both signs are fixed, so both hang on to a feeling long after it's stopped helping. Your Moon is fire and the card is water, and what warms you and what the card stirs up don't sit easily in the same body.

From the inside it can feel like a hunger for attention you're slightly ashamed of. You imagine being chosen, the message saying you were the one they thought of, the party thrown for you, and some nights that picture is sweeter than anything that actually happened in the day. Venus has no special dignity in Leo and follows the Sun, so when you're low it wants warmth and applause, and quickly. Scorpio's pull is slower and more secretive, toward one person seeing all of you. You may want both at once and feel unable to say either out loud.

With a partner, watch for testing them, going quiet to see if they notice. With children, or with something you've made, you'll pour warmth in and feel it badly if nothing comes back. Sleep can run late while you replay a conversation. Ask someone close for the particular kind of attention you're missing, even if it feels childish to name it.
moon.reversed:
Pride can wall off a Leo Moon when this card turns over. You feel overlooked and, in place of saying so, retreat into a private story where you're the wronged one and everyone will be sorry eventually. Your fire and the card's water don't mix, and here the water puts the warmth out, so you go cool and dignified and privately furious. Two fixed signs at a square make climbing down very hard.

At home it shows up as a long silence over a small slight. With friends it can be skipping the dinner because they didn't make enough fuss last time. You might also treat yourself lavishly to make up for the missing attention, a new jacket, a big night out. Say the plain sentence, 'I felt left out', to the person it's about.

rising.upright:
Leo rising comes into a room with the lights on, and people look. With the Seven of Cups drawn for your mask, they're also imagining things about you, a glamorous life, a lot of admirers, some secret plan. The Sun rules your chart, and Venus, a guest in Leo with no rank of its own, falls in with the Sun's style, so the card's allure is showy and easy to spot from the other side of a room.

Count whole signs from Leo and Scorpio lands on your fourth house, home and family and the private ground under your feet. That's where this card's longing comes from, and it squares your rising sign. So the confident front goes out into the world while something at home, or something old from childhood, pulls the other way. Fire meeting water gives you plenty of warmth on the surface and a damp patch underneath that strangers can't see. You might notice you're saying yes to invitations partly so you don't have to be at home.

Socially you'll be good company and slightly hard to know, which draws people in. At work, clients may buy the vision without checking the detail, so check it yourself. At home there might be a family matter you keep talking around. Turn down one evening out and deal with whatever's waiting in the house.
rising.reversed:
Charm turns into costume for Leo rising when this card is upside down. You dress the part, tell the good version, make sure the photos look right, and anyone who knows you can see the effort. Venus goes along with the Sun in Leo, and it hates being caught trying. Scorpio sits on your fourth house and squares your rising, so the gap between the public face and what's going on at home gets harder to hide.

New people are the ones most taken in, and you can feel lonely in a crowd who only know the front. At work you might be promising a launch that isn't ready. At home someone may be tired of hearing about plans that never reach the kitchen table. Let one new acquaintance see an ordinary, unimpressive part of your week.

sun.upright:
Venus is in fall in Virgo, which in plain terms means the planet of pleasure doesn't get much of a hearing in your sign. It has to work sideways, through being useful and getting things right. That makes this an odd card for a Virgo Sun to draw, all longing and possibility, the sort of wanting you'd normally file under things to deal with later.

Scorpio sextiles Virgo, though, a cooperative angle, an opening that's there if you use it. From the inside, what usually happens is that your critical eye goes to work on the cups. You rank them, research them, find the flaw in each, and end up with a spreadsheet of seven futures and no appetite for any of them. I've watched Virgo Suns do this with a career change for years. Desire in your sign comes in through a side door, dressed up as a sensible reason, the course that's useful, the flat that's an investment. If you were born between ten and nineteen degrees of Virgo, Venus rules your decan, the Nine of Pentacles, and you probably have more room for plain enjoyment than you let on.

In the job, notice whether the thing you keep fixing is the thing you'd actually like to be doing. With money, a treat may need a justification before you'll allow it. In the body it can show up as a busy kind of tiredness, on the go all day and never rested. Choose one of the seven for no reason except that you'd enjoy it.
sun.reversed:
Turned over, the card can have a Virgo Sun talking itself out of every cup before touching one. Each wish gets a list of reasons against, and they're very good lists. Venus in fall can't get a word in, so what's left is competence with the pleasure taken out, and a flat sense of having been sensible for too long.

At work you may be the one everyone relies on and nobody thinks to reward, partly because you've never asked. In a relationship you could be tidying and fixing when your partner just wants you to sit down with them. Money saved for one day can sit there for a decade. Spend a small, silly amount on something with no use at all and don't explain it to anyone.

moon.upright:
Virgo Moons feel safer when things are in order, the bench wiped, the bills paid, the plan written down somewhere. This card is a jumble of options floating in cloud, and your first reaction may be to sort them into piles. Your Moon is earth and the card is water, two elements that feed each other, so a longing here can settle into something real if it's given time.

What makes it uncomfortable is Venus being in fall in your Moon's sign. Comfort and pleasure go unheard in Virgo and have to get their way indirectly, so when you want something you might feel it as worry first. You can't tell if you're anxious or just hungry for something nicer in your life. The sextile between Scorpio and Virgo helps, a friendly angle that works once you take it up. Under the fretting there's often a very specific wish, a quieter job, a softer bedroom, a friend you've lost touch with, and you'll find it if you stop tidying long enough to hear it.

Appetite and sleep are often the first places a buried want shows, restless nights, picking at meals. At home you may find yourself reorganising a cupboard at eleven at night. With a friend or partner, you might offer help when what you'd actually like is company. When the worry starts up, write down what you'd want if it didn't have to be sensible, and read it again in the morning.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the card can turn a Virgo Moon's care into criticism of yourself for wanting anything at all. You have a daydream, you go through it for flaws, and then you tell yourself off for having it. Venus in fall can't argue back, so the wish gets filed as silly and the feeling goes underground, where it becomes low-level anxiety about nothing in particular.

In the daily routine it shows as over-control, the same meals, the same list, no room for a nice surprise. With a partner you could end up picking at small things because the big thing is too hard to say. Your shoulders may be up round your ears by evening. Pick one small comfort and have it without doing a job first to earn it.

rising.upright:
Mercury rules Virgo rising, so you usually meet the world a little reserved and very observant, the person who spots the typo on the menu. The Seven of Cups gives that careful front a softer, dreamier edge. Strangers may find you harder to read, a bit wistful, as if part of you is somewhere else.

In whole-sign houses Scorpio is your third, the house of everyday talk, siblings and short trips across town. That's where this card sits for you, and it sextiles your rising, so the opening is real if you take it. You might find you're saying more than usual, or saying it with feeling where you'd normally be precise. Venus is in fall in Virgo, so charm doesn't come easily at a first meeting. It turns up in the conversation afterwards instead, the message you send on the bus home. People will read possibilities into what you say, and some of them you meant.

With a brother or sister, an old conversation may reopen and go more gently this time. At work an email you wrote with a bit of feeling in it could get a warmer reply than usual. On the commute you'll notice more and drift off more. Before you send the next heartfelt message, read it once and ask if you'd say it to their face.
rising.reversed:
Over-explaining is the usual trap for Virgo rising with this card reversed. Every new person gets the full set of caveats, how you're not really sure, how it might not work, and the dreamy side the card offers is buried under qualifications. Scorpio on your third house and Venus in fall in your rising sign put easy charm out of reach, so you fill the gap with detail.

At work it can be a pitch that sinks under its own footnotes. In dating, you may talk yourself down on a first date before the other person has had a chance to like you. With a neighbour or a sibling it's the message drafted six times and never sent. Next time you describe something you want, say it in one sentence and stop.

sun.upright:
Libra is one of the two signs Venus rules, so a Libra Sun has the card's planet for its own. In this card, though, Venus has gone next door into Scorpio, where it's in detriment and has to work against its own nature. The two signs are neighbours, a semi-sextile, and each has what the other lacks. You've got the grace and the sense of fairness. Scorpio has the appetite and the nerve.

That's why this card can leave a Libra Sun feeling slightly off. You're used to weighing things up, which suits seven cups very well to begin with. Then the weighing doesn't stop. Each option is lovely in its way and each would disappoint somebody, and you want the one that pleases everyone, which among seven doesn't exist. Air and water haven't been introduced, so your reasoning and your feelings keep passing each other in the hall. The Scorpio side brings up wants you'd prefer not to look at, jealousy, a hunger for something with more bite to it.

In a relationship it can look like imagining other lives with other people. Usually nothing's wrong, the card has just stirred the question up. At work it's the offer that looks elegant against the one that pays, and you can't pick. With friends, you may be keeping the peace on a subject you feel strongly about. Say the strong view to one person and see what happens.
sun.reversed:
For a Libra Sun, this card reversed is often indecision that's gone on so long it's become a kind of decision. You've kept two or three cups in the air for a year to keep everyone happy, and the people waiting on you have started to give up. Venus is your ruler and it's in detriment in the card's sign, so the fairness you're proud of can harden into never committing to anything.

In love, someone may be waiting to hear what you want long term. At work there might be a role you've half accepted and half turned down. With friends it's the holiday you're still working out. Set a date, write it somewhere you'll see it, and choose by then even if the choice is imperfect.

moon.upright:
Harmony is what calms a Libra Moon. A pleasant room, people getting on, a partner in a good mood. The Seven of Cups brings the Venus you know, your own ruler, except it's come over from Scorpio next door and brought Scorpio's intensity with it. Wants you'd normally smooth over come up stronger and stay longer.

The semi-sextile between the two signs is a neighbourly, slightly awkward angle, a shared fence and not much else. Water and air are neutral, so the feelings don't clash with your need for calm, they just don't obey it either. You may catch yourself daydreaming about a more passionate life, a romance out of a film, a house that's beautiful in every room, and then feeling guilty because what you've got is actually fine. That guilt is very Libra. So is checking a feeling against what other people would think before you let yourself have it.

With a partner, you may want more depth and more honesty and be scared it'll spoil the peace. At home you might keep rearranging the furniture or buying lovely things to settle a feeling that has nothing to do with the room. Sleep can be fine until something unresolved surfaces late. Tell your partner one thing you've been keeping pleasant, and let it be a bit awkward.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, this card can keep a Libra Moon in a very pretty fog. You're fine, everything's lovely, you'd rather not talk about it, and underneath is a longing you won't look at because it might upset someone. A Libra Moon can keep this up for a surprisingly long time, because it's so good at looking content. Venus rules your Moon's sign and struggles in Scorpio, and here it turns wanting into people-pleasing.

At home you may be keeping a partner happy at the cost of saying what you need. Money can go on beautiful things that lift the mood for an afternoon. With friends you might agree to plans you don't want and come home drained. When someone asks what you'd like, answer before you check their face.

rising.upright:
Libra rising has Venus for a chart ruler, so first impressions come easily to you. You're pleasant, well put together, good at making the other person feel like the only one in the room. This card is your own ruler sitting in Scorpio, the next sign along, and in whole-sign houses Scorpio is your second, the house of money and what you value.

So the charm is on show as usual, and underneath it you're weighing up what you're worth and what you'd like to own. Venus in detriment has to work harder, and in the second house that can make you very aware of price tags, yours and other people's. People may assume from how you carry yourself that you're richer, or more relaxed about money, or surer of your value. The semi-sextile between Libra and Scorpio means these two parts of you are neighbours without much to say to each other, the easy manner at the door and the anxious sums behind it.

In business you'll make a good first impression, so use it to ask for a proper rate. Shopping, watch for buying the look of the person you'd like to be. With someone new, notice if you're working out what they're worth to you before you've really met them. Next time you name a price or a salary, add ten per cent and don't apologise for it.
rising.reversed:
When the card turns over, Libra rising can sell itself short to keep things nice. You drop the price, agree to the terms, laugh off the comment, because the pleasant first impression matters that much to you. Your ruler is in detriment in Scorpio, your second-house sign, so your sense of your own worth takes the hit behind the smile.

Money is where it shows first, in discounts you offered without being asked. At work you may be liked by everyone and paid less than the colleague who complains. Friends may borrow and forget, and you'll say nothing. In a new relationship you might shape yourself to their taste far too quickly. Next time you hear yourself saying that's fine, wait three seconds and say what would actually suit you.

sun.upright:
This is one of Scorpio's own cards. The last ten degrees of your sign belong to Venus in the old decan scheme, and this card stands for that slice, so a Scorpio Sun drawing it is being shown something from inside its own sign. If your birthday falls in that last stretch, it's your decan card as well. Venus is in detriment in Scorpio, living opposite its own house, and the strain shows.

You'll recognise that strain. Scorpio Suns don't want things casually. When you want something it's whole-body, the job, the person, the secret, the score to settle, and water on water means nothing in this pairing turns the volume down. Have a look at the cup with the shrouded figure in it, the one whose face you can't make out. That's the kind of want this card raises in you, a thing you're drawn to partly because you can't see all of it. Mars, your sign's traditional ruler, gives you the drive to go after it. Venus being in detriment means it may not bring the pleasure you pictured, and part of you already suspects that.

At work you might fix on one goal, a role, a rival's job, with a force that surprises people. In love the pull can be toward someone unavailable, or toward a closeness your partner isn't offering. With money, there may be a bold bet that feels like fate. Before you commit, find out the one thing about it you've been avoiding finding out.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun with this card reversed can fix on one cup so hard the others stop existing. The fixation feels like loyalty, or like knowing your own mind, and it's a lot of Scorpio concentrated in one place, with Venus in detriment turning pleasure into possession. You may not even enjoy the thing much. You just can't stop wanting it.

It shows in the ex you still check on, the grudge at work you're quietly feeding, the investment you won't sell. Friends may have stopped raising it. In the body it can feel like a clenched jaw and shallow sleep. Take one day where you deliberately don't look it up, don't check, don't plan, and notice how much of you it's been using.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon trusts slowly and feels everything at depth, usually without letting on. The card is native to your Moon's sign, one of its three decan cards, and it's water meeting water, so it doesn't have to knock. It walks in and turns up whatever was already going on.

Mostly what it turns up is longing, and not the light kind. You might find yourself imagining a different life in close detail, or thinking about a person you shouldn't, or replaying an old betrayal and rewriting how you'd handle it. Venus is in detriment here, so comfort and pleasure are hard to come by in your Moon's sign. You don't soothe easily, and the card's daydreams can start to feel like the only soft place going. Some of what you picture is useful, because it points at what's missing. Some of it is a loop, and you'll know which by whether you feel better or worse after an hour in it.

Sleep is often where it shows, vivid dreams or lying awake with one face in mind. With a partner there may be a need for honesty you haven't voiced, or a jealousy you're keeping very quiet. With money, you may want the security of something put aside that nobody knows about. Tell one person you trust the daydream in full, including the embarrassing part.
moon.reversed:
When a Scorpio Moon meets this card upside down, the private fantasy becomes a hiding place with a lock on the door. You're hurt, you say nothing, and you spend the evenings inside a detailed story about what you'd say or do if you let yourself. Water on water keeps it deep, and with Venus uncomfortable in your sign, the ways you treat yourself don't really comfort you.

It shows up as checking someone's online life at night, or grazing well past the point of enjoying it. At work you might be civil and very cold with the person who hurt you. With family, an old wound may be replaying in the background. Let one person in on what's really bothering you, and let them see it before you've tidied it up.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising already comes across as a bit of a mystery. People sense something going on behind the eyes and can't quite place it. This card is one of your rising sign's own decans, which puts it squarely on your first house, and that sense of hidden depth gets stronger.

Mars rules your chart in the traditional scheme, and Venus is in detriment in your rising sign, so charm doesn't come out sweet. It comes out as intensity, a look held a second too long, a question that goes past small talk. Water on water amplifies. Strangers may read a great deal into you that you never put there, a secret, an attraction, a plan, and some will be drawn in by it. Your instinct is to start things quietly and watch first, and with this card you might end up watching several doors and not walking through any, because each one could be a trap.

At work you'll be trusted with confidential things, maybe more of them than you'd like. In dating, people may project a fantasy onto you that you never signed up for. Your style might go darker or more private, sunglasses on a grey day. When someone new seems to have decided who you are, correct one detail early.
rising.reversed:
Mystery becomes a shield for Scorpio rising with this card reversed. You give nothing away, you let people wonder, and the wondering keeps them at a safe distance. Venus in detriment makes warmth harder to show at a first meeting, so you lean on intrigue to cover for it. Mars ruling your chart helps you hold your ground, and it can also make you guarded to the point of seeming cold.

New colleagues may find you hard to approach. In dating, a match might lose interest because they can't tell what you want. It can also show as keeping your options secret, one conversation here and another there. Some of the people you've kept guessing would have been worth letting in. Tell someone new one plain fact about yourself they didn't expect.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns like to have a horizon, a plan for next year, a place they haven't been yet. You'd think seven glowing cups would suit you, and in some ways they do. Jupiter rules your sign, and Venus, which holds no special rank in Sagittarius, takes on Jupiter's appetite and generosity there, so the wanting in this card comes in large. Bigger house, longer trip, the degree you never finished.

The catch is that the card belongs to Scorpio, the sign just behind yours, a semi-sextile, two neighbours with little in common. Scorpio tends to want one thing and go all the way down into it, and you'd usually prefer to keep moving. Add fire against water and there's steam, a restlessness that heats up without going anywhere. It can feel like having the whole world on offer and a strange heaviness about picking any of it. Some of that heaviness is Scorpio asking what you're running from. Sagittarians are honest to a fault with other people and fairly good at dodging that question with themselves.

In study it's the brochures and the half-planned move overseas. At work, a big vision may need a smaller first step than you'd like. In love, you might be imagining freedom while also wanting someone to stay. Pick the option that scares you a little and find out one practical fact about it, a price, a date, a name.
sun.reversed:
Leaving is how this card reversed tends to look for a Sagittarius Sun. The big trip, the new course, the fresh start in another city, each one a cup that promises everything, and each conveniently far from whatever you'd have to face if you stayed put. Jupiter colours Venus in your sign, and upside down that becomes more, bigger, further, with very little actually felt.

Friends may notice there's a new plan every time they see you. Money can leak into bookings you later cancel. At work, a transfer or a new role may look like the answer when the trouble is closer to home. In love there may be someone you keep at arm's length by talking about the future. Stay put for one uncomfortable conversation before you book anything else.

moon.upright:
Freedom soothes a Sagittarius Moon. Room to move, a window open, somewhere to go at the weekend. Your usual way with a heavy feeling is to get out, go for a drive, book something, laugh it off. The Seven of Cups brings a watery, clinging sort of longing to a fire Moon, and those two elements are opposed, so this time the feeling tends to come along for the ride.

Scorpio sits right behind Sagittarius, a semi-sextile, the sign you've just come from. Each has what the other hasn't. You've got the optimism and it's got the depth. Venus is only a guest in your sign, with no dignity there, and it borrows Jupiter's hopefulness, so the daydreams are generous and a bit grand. What catches you out is how emotional they are. You might feel homesick for a place you've never been, or keep thinking about someone from years ago. For a Moon that prefers to keep things light, it's unsettling, and you may be short with people without knowing why.

Sleep may be restless, full of long travelling dreams. In a friendship you might want more closeness and not know how to ask for it. With money there's a temptation to buy yourself the feeling of escape, a ticket, a weekend away. Sit with the heavy feeling for ten minutes before deciding what to do about it.
moon.reversed:
Bolting is the risk for a Sagittarius Moon with this card reversed. Something hurts and you're already out the door, on a trip, into a new hobby, keen on a new crowd. Jupiter's optimism, borrowed by Venus in your sign, tells you the next place will be better. Fire and water pull against each other here, and the fire wins by leaving. The feeling waits for you.

It tends to show as a string of plans that each last about a fortnight. With money, it's flights booked late at night. With a partner it may be jokes where there should be a serious talk, and they'll notice even if they laugh. Your body can feel wired and worn out at once. Next time you want to leave, say out loud what you'd be leaving, then decide.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising tends to meet people with a big laugh and an open door. Jupiter runs your chart, and the Seven of Cups on your mask makes that impression brighter still. Strangers see someone full of plans and good stories, the sort of person who might be off to Peru on a whim.

Scorpio is the sign behind your rising, which makes it your twelfth house, the house of what's hidden, private retreat, the things you don't show. The card's longing sits there for you. So you're all cheer at the front door, and behind it something quieter is going on, a wish you haven't told anyone, a feeling you're keeping to yourself. Venus has no rank in Sagittarius and follows Jupiter's lead, so your charm is generous and open-handed. The semi-sextile means your public manner and your private longing don't have much to say to each other, and fire and water are opposed on top of that.

At work, people may assume you're up for anything. In dating, someone could fall for the adventurer when what you're privately after is some peace. With friends you'll be great company and then gone early, and some of them will wonder why. Watch whether you're running on enthusiasm and skipping rest. Spend one evening alone with no plans and see what comes up.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising with the card reversed can overpromise with a grin. The trip you'll organise, the introduction you'll make, the favour you'll definitely do. People like you on the spot and feel let down a month later. Venus follows Jupiter in your sign, and upside down that generosity runs well ahead of your diary. With Scorpio on your twelfth house, the reason you're scattering yourself is often hidden, even from you.

At work it can be taking on projects to seem keen and then vanishing. Socially it's the party where you promised three people a proper catch-up. Someone you met recently may already have a story about you that isn't true. Privately you may be exhausted and hiding it well. Keep a note of what you've offered people and cancel one thing with an honest reason.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns plan in years. You know what you're building and roughly when it'll be done, so a card full of floating possibilities can look like a waste of an afternoon. But Scorpio sextiles Capricorn, an easy, cooperative angle, and earth and water are good for each other. This card's more use to you than it looks.

Venus has no special dignity in Capricorn and takes on Saturn's seriousness there, so your wants usually come dressed as goals, the partnership, the property, the title. What the card does is show you a couple of wants that have no business case at all, and you may not know what to do with them. I've seen plenty of Capricorn Suns keep a dream in a drawer for twenty years because it wasn't practical. The other side of it is the ambitious cups, the jewels and the laurel wreath, which might be things you want because they're expected of you.

At work, check that the next rung up is really where you want to go. With money, a small amount spent on something purely for pleasure will do you real good. With a parent, there may be an old expectation still doing the steering. Write down the dream you've put off longest and put a real date next to it.
sun.reversed:
Discipline aimed at the wrong cup is how a Capricorn Sun tends to meet this card reversed. You've picked the respectable dream and you're climbing toward it steadily, and something in you has gone flat. Venus takes on Saturn's weight in your sign, and with the card upside down, pleasure gets postponed until a retirement that keeps moving further off. The body may feel stiff and held in, tired in a way sleep doesn't touch.

Work is where it shows, long hours for a goal that stopped thrilling you a while ago. In a relationship you might be dependable and unavailable at the same time. Your partner may be missing the person you were before the plan. Friends may have quietly stopped inviting you. Book one thing purely for fun, pay for it, and go.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safe when things are handled. Bills paid, plans made, nobody falling apart. Feelings are allowed, but they wait their turn. This is a card of longing and daydreams, which isn't normally on your agenda, but earth and water are friendly elements and Scorpio makes a sextile to Capricorn, so there's an opening if you'll use it.

Venus is a guest in Capricorn with no dignity, and it takes on Saturn's reserve, so what comforts you tends to be solid and slightly austere. A good coat. Money in the bank. When this card turns up, softer and less sensible wants come with it, a wish to be looked after, a daydream about stopping work, a longing for somebody who'll notice how tired you are. You may feel embarrassed by them and push them back down. They tend to come back at night, when you're too tired to push.

In the body, tiredness may be the loudest signal you've got. With a parent, especially a strict one, old feelings could stir. At work you might daydream about walking out, and then stay late anyway. With money, you might picture a very different, easier life and then go back to the spreadsheet. Let someone look after you in one small way and don't pay them back.
moon.reversed:
Self-reliance can go too far for a Capricorn Moon when this card is reversed. You won't admit to wanting anything, so the wants go underground and come out as cynicism about other people's dreams. The daydream about a softer life gets dismissed as nonsense before it's finished. With Saturn colouring Venus in Capricorn, comfort gets rationed until there's hardly any left.

At home you may be the one holding it all together, and quietly resentful about it. With a partner, affection may come out as practical help when they'd like something warmer. At work you might take on more to avoid feeling anything. Say to someone close, 'I'd like to be looked after for a bit', and see what they do.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising usually comes across as capable and slightly formal, the one people assume is in charge. Saturn rules your chart. With this card drawn for your mask, there's something less easy to read about you, a hint of dreaminess, or an ambition beyond the obvious one, and people wonder what you're after.

Scorpio is your eleventh-house sign, the house of friends, networks and hopes, and the card's longing gathers there. It makes a sextile to your rising, a helpful angle that still needs using. So your instinct at the start of anything is to think about who you know, which group you might join, what the long hope is. Venus is a visitor in Capricorn and takes on Saturn's caution, so your charm is dry and understated. People who meet you may not realise how much you're hoping for, and you might not tell them.

Through work contacts you may be offered several doors at once, and some are better on paper. With friends, a new group could look exciting and turn out shallow, or look dull and be the real thing. Your style might soften a little, a colour you'd usually pass over. Tell one friend what you're really hoping for over the next few years.
rising.reversed:
Ambition on the outside and hopes kept hidden, that's Capricorn rising with this card upside down. People see the competent front and assume you've got it all planned, when privately you're unsure which of several paths to take. Scorpio on your eleventh house puts the uncertainty around friends and future hopes, and Saturn's reserve stops you asking anyone. Venus follows Saturn here and keeps its warmth for later, which can be a long time coming.

At work you might network hard with people you don't much like. Socially, a friendship can drift because you never quite say you value it. You could end up in a group for how it looks. Put some real time into one friendship, the kind of time that does nothing for your career.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns tend to want things for everyone. A better system, a fairer arrangement, a future that works. The Seven of Cups brings a much more private kind of wanting, Scorpio's kind, and Scorpio squares Aquarius, two fixed signs three apart, friction that won't let either of them settle. If you were born in the opening decan of Aquarius, nought to nine degrees, Venus rules it through the Five of Swords, so the card isn't a complete stranger to you.

Venus holds no rank in your sign and takes on Saturn's coolness, or Uranus's oddness if you use the modern ruler, so you're used to your desires feeling slightly detached, interesting ideas more than cravings. This card asks for something you don't always enjoy giving. Air and water haven't been introduced, and your head can't quite get hold of what it stirs up, a personal longing, a jealousy, a want that isn't noble at all. Being fixed, you can defend your principles for a long time while a very human wish sits there unexamined.

In a friendship, you may want to be someone's favourite and feel silly about it. At work, a cause you're attached to might also be feeding a need to be recognised. With a partner there may be a closeness you want and keep intellectualising. Admit the unfashionable want to yourself, plainly, and leave it there for a while.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with this card reversed can hold out for an ideal nobody could meet. The perfect project, the perfect community, the partner who agrees about everything. Real options keep falling short and you keep stepping back. Venus borrows Saturn's detachment in your sign, so the disappointment doesn't look like disappointment. It looks like being above it all. The square with Scorpio keeps the pressure on, and being fixed, you'd prefer to stay principled and alone.

It shows in groups you join and quietly leave. At work a brilliant idea can stay a document for years. In love you might keep someone at a distance because they don't match the ideal you drew up. Choose one flawed, real thing and give it a year.

moon.upright:
Space is what settles an Aquarius Moon. A bit of distance from the feeling, a chance to think it through, friends around and nobody too close. This card doesn't give you that. It's water, and it comes from Scorpio, which squares Aquarius, two fixed signs at a stubborn angle.

Air and water are neutral to each other, which sounds harmless, but it means you have no ready way of handling what comes up. And what comes up can be intense, a longing for someone, a fantasy of being truly known, a stab of jealousy that seems out of character. Venus has no dignity in your sign and borrows Saturn's reserve, so your usual comfort is detachment. With this card, the detachment works less well. You might find yourself daydreaming about a different life and feeling oddly guilty, as if wanting something just for you were a betrayal of your principles.

Sleep might be broken by thoughts you can't switch off. With friends you may feel lonely in a group you usually love. With a partner you might want reassurance and not know how to ask without feeling needy. With money, you could find yourself giving to a cause when what you wanted was a hug. Try naming the feeling to one friend as a feeling, without explaining it or making it interesting.
moon.reversed:
Cold is the usual direction for an Aquarius Moon when this card is reversed. A feeling arrives that you don't like, a longing or a jealousy, and you step so far back from it that you start describing yourself like a case study. The square with Scorpio keeps pressing, and being fixed you keep resisting. It can also look like a sudden fascination with some cause or project, all head, while the actual hurt goes untouched.

In friendships it can look like pulling away without explaining. With a partner you might go vague and busy just as they want closeness. Your body may feel restless and underslept. Next time you catch yourself analysing a feeling, stop and notice where in your body it is.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising usually meets people friendly and a little detached, more interested in their ideas than their gossip. Saturn rules your chart in the old scheme. With the Seven of Cups as your mask, you may come across as more of a dreamer, someone with an unusual plan or a vision people can't quite follow.

On a whole-sign chart Scorpio sits at the top for you, your tenth house, career and public reputation. The card's longing lands there, and it squares your rising sign. So you're meeting people with your usual easy, offbeat manner, and behind it there's a very serious wish about your work and how you're seen. Venus borrows Saturn's style in Aquarius, so the charm is cool. The square makes friction that pushes you to act. You might catch yourself scrolling job listings on your lunch break, or describing a career you haven't started as if it's already real.

At work, people may see an ambition in you that you haven't declared. In a new group you could be cast as the visionary. With a boss or mentor, there may be a gap between what they think you want and what you actually want. Tell someone who's in a position to help one specific thing you want from your work.
rising.reversed:
Detachment can read as indifference when Aquarius rising gets this card reversed. Behind it, Scorpio on your tenth house is stirring up a career wish you're not ready to own, and it's easier to seem above it all. Venus follows Saturn's coolness in your sign, so warmth at a first meeting takes effort you'd sooner not spend. The square keeps the tension on, and you're a fixed sign, so you won't budge.

At work you might underplay what you're after and watch others get the chances. A new manager may assume you're content where you are. Networking, a clever manner can put off the very people who could help you. Friends may think you're vague about your future when you're anything but. Say out loud, to one person with some influence, what you're actually aiming for.

sun.upright:
Venus is exalted in Pisces, which means the planet of love and beauty is an honoured guest in your sign, shown at its most idealised. So a Pisces Sun has an unusual relationship with this card. It's Venus in Scorpio, in detriment, wanting hard and not quite trusting what it wants. You carry the higher, dreamier version of that same planet, and the card hands you the heavier one.

Scorpio is a trine from Pisces, both water, so the card flows into you with almost no resistance. That's lovely, and it's also the problem. Same element, same language, and nothing to put the brakes on. You can look at all seven cups glowing and believe in every one of them, the perfect partner, the calling, the rescue, the escape. Pisces Suns are generous with belief. What the card asks is whether some of those cups hold other people's dreams you've taken on as your own, because you do have a way of absorbing wants that were never yours.

At work, a creative or helping role might sound perfect in the description. In love, someone's potential may look very bright indeed. With money, generosity can run ahead of what's in the account. Take the dream you're most sure of and ask one grounded friend to poke holes in it.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun meeting this card reversed can drift. Every cup looks equally good, so you wait for a sign, and the sign doesn't come, and meanwhile the years go by in a very pleasant fog. You might tell yourself it's patience. Venus exalted in your sign idealises everything, and the trine from Scorpio pours in more longing and more maybes with nothing solid to hold them.

In love it can look like waiting for someone to change. At work it's the creative project that's always about to start. With money, it can mean trusting someone's plan without checking it. Family may have stopped asking what you're doing next. Take one practical step toward one dream without waiting to feel ready.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks up the feelings of everyone in the room and needs time alone to wring them out again. The Seven of Cups shares your Moon's element and sits a trine away, and Venus, the card's planet, is exalted in Pisces. It's about as easy a fit as this card gets, which is lovely, and it also means nothing slows it down.

What it feels like is rich, dreamy inner weather. Longing for somewhere else, memories that feel present, imagined conversations that go perfectly. Jupiter rules your sign, with Neptune as the modern ruler, and the card's daydreams pick up that boundlessness. You may find it hard to tell intuition from a wish. Some of it is intuition. Some of it is your mind decorating an ordinary feeling, and being a Pisces Moon you won't always know which until later, and that's fine.

Sleep is likely to be full of dreams, and you may need more of it. With friends, you might take on someone's troubles as if they were yours. With a partner, you may be imagining a deeper bond and feel a little let down by the real one. Spend an hour on your own doing something with your hands, and notice what the feeling is when you come back to it.
moon.reversed:
Escape can start to look like rest for a Pisces Moon when this card turns over. A long bath, a whole series, a daydream that takes up most of the evening, each fine on its own, and together a way of never quite being here. Venus exalted in Pisces loves the dream, and water on water means there's nothing in the pairing to call you back.

It shows in missed messages and the sense of having lost a week somewhere. With someone close, you might promise things from inside the dream and forget them outside it. Your body may feel heavy and slow to start. Keep one real, grounding routine, a walk at the same time each day, and don't let the dream talk you out of it.

rising.upright:
People meeting Pisces rising often feel understood before they've finished a sentence. You look like you'd understand, and usually you would. Jupiter rules your chart in the old scheme, Neptune in the modern one, and the Seven of Cups turns that soft, receptive first impression right up. Strangers may project their dreams onto you with alarming ease.

By whole sign, Scorpio is your ninth house, travel, study, belief and the long view. That's where this card's longing sits, a trine from your rising, so it comes in easily. You may meet the world with an unusual interest in far-off places or big ideas, a wish to study something or go somewhere. Venus is exalted in Pisces, so charm comes naturally, and people will read romance or spirituality into you. The risk is that everyone sees what they want and you let them.

In study, a course or teacher may look like the answer to everything. Travelling, you'll be easy to talk to and easy to sell to. With colleagues you might find yourself the one people tell their troubles to at the coffee machine, which is kind of you and exhausting by Friday. In dating, someone may cast you as their muse. When a new acquaintance seems certain about who you are, ask what they're basing it on.
rising.reversed:
This card reversed can make Pisces rising into a mirror. People see their fantasy in you, and you reflect it back because that's easier than showing what's really there. It feels like kindness. Venus exalted in your rising sign makes you charming, and the trine to Scorpio in your ninth house brings in grand ideas about belief, travel, a teacher or a cause, none of them tested.

It can show up as signing up for a retreat or course that promises too much. In dating, it may be becoming whoever they wanted. At work, you might say yes to a role that sounded inspiring and turns out to be a hard slog. In the next conversation where you'd usually nod, say one thing you disagree with.

1.upright:
Several versions of you tend to be floating about when the Seven of Cups falls in the first house. A new look, a new role at work, a fresh start somewhere nobody knows you. This is the house of the body, the face, how you walk into a room and how you begin anything, and it's angular, a corner of the chart, so what happens here gets seen.

The friction is that the first house is Aries ground, Mars's territory, and Venus is in detriment in Aries just as it is in Scorpio. So the card's way of wanting, slow and deep and hard to pin down, runs against a house that wants to get going. Water and fire are opposed, and Scorpio and Aries sit a quincunx apart, five signs, forever making small adjustments to each other. From the inside it's like trying on selves in the mirror and not settling on one. You change your hair and change it back. You introduce yourself one way at work and another way at the pub.

In the body, energy may come and go with your mood, keen one day and flat the next. At work you could be trying to decide how you'd like to be seen, as the reliable one or the one with ideas. With someone new, you may be showing a version of yourself that's partly wishful. Pick one thing about how you present yourself and keep it steady long enough to see what it does for you.
1.reversed:
Picturing a better self can crowd out looking after this one when the card is reversed in the first house. Sleep, food and movement slip, because a big overhaul is being planned and hasn't started. The first house is Aries ground and wants action, and upside down the card hands it daydreams in place of a first step. People may find you hard to read, as if you're half somewhere else.

It shows in the gym membership, the wardrobe you're about to replace, the fresh start that's always next Monday. At work you might hang back from putting yourself forward until you're the finished version. Do one small physical thing for yourself every day, a walk, a proper breakfast, and let the overhaul wait.

2.upright:
Money and what you think you're worth, those are the second house, and it's Venus's own ground, since Venus rules Taurus, the house's natural sign. So the card's planet is on home turf here, and money and desire get tangled up together. Drawn into the second, this card tends to bring several ways of earning or spending into view at once.

Scorpio is the sign opposite Taurus, the same axis seen from the other end. Taurus wants to own things and enjoy them. Scorpio wants to merge, share and gamble, and the card pulls you toward that end, where money gets bound up with feeling and power and things you'd love to have. Earth and water get along, so some of these ideas can grow into something that lasts, given time. The seven cups in this house are mostly about money, though. A second income, a big purchase, a scheme promising a return. A few of them are sound. A couple would cost you a lot and give very little back.

With the budget, you may catch yourself browsing big purchases you haven't priced properly. At work an offer or a pay rise could look better on paper than in practice, so read the terms. With self-worth, you might be comparing yourself with people whose lives only look good from the outside. Put actual numbers against the three biggest things you want, and see which still appeal.
2.reversed:
Money going out on feelings is the usual shape of this card reversed in the second house. A bad day and something gets bought. A wish for a different life and a course gets paid for. Venus is at home in this house and uncomfortable in the card's sign, so your sense of what things are worth, including you, gets skewed.

It shows in the bank statement, in subscriptions you forgot about, and in a quiet feeling that you're worth less than people think. At work you might be undercharging and telling yourself it's temporary. A partner may be worried about shared spending and not know how to raise it. Go through the last three months of spending with a highlighter and mark what you'd buy again.

3.upright:
Everyday talk lives in the third house, the messages, the siblings, the neighbours, the short trips and whatever you're learning. It's a cadent house, one where things get processed and adjusted, and the Moon has its joy here, so it's already busy and changeable. With this card in it, your conversations fill up with what might be.

Gemini is this house's natural sign, and Scorpio is a quincunx from Gemini, five signs apart with nothing much in common. Water and air are neutral and have to be introduced. So the card's deep, private kind of wanting comes into a house built for quick, light exchange, and it doesn't always fit. You might find yourself sending long, heartfelt messages, or dropping a hint in a group chat that's bigger than it looks. Several books get started at once, several courses bookmarked. Talk comes easily, and talk about what might happen comes easiest of all.

With a sibling, you may be picturing a closer relationship than you've got and wanting to reach out. Around the neighbourhood, you might daydream about moving, or about who lives behind that particular door. In learning, it's a pile of half-read books by the bed. Finish the one you've got furthest with before you open another.
3.reversed:
Words that promise more than they deliver, that's the third house with this card reversed. You say you'll call, you say you'll come, you describe a plan in glowing detail, and none of it happens. Most of it is meant kindly. The quincunx between Scorpio and Gemini keeps what you feel and what you say slightly out of step, and the gap shows.

With a sibling or a neighbour, a misunderstanding may grow because nobody said the plain thing. Your inbox may be full of messages you meant to answer properly. Study can suffer too, notes taken and never looked at. On short trips you might be distracted enough to miss the turn, or the train. Answer the three oldest messages with something short and true, and don't promise anything in them.

4.upright:
Home, family, where you come from and the private ground you go back to, that's the fourth house. It's angular, a corner of the chart, so what goes on here carries weight. Its natural sign is Cancer, ruled by the Moon, and Scorpio makes a trine to Cancer, so this card settles into the house with no trouble at all.

That ease is mixed. Water on water amplifies, for better and for too much. You may find yourself imagining different homes, a bigger place, a move to the coast, a family get-together where everybody behaves, and the feelings attached to each are strong. Old family memories can surface, some sweet and some sore.
