Venus wants beauty and closeness at home, and in Scorpio it wants depth, so underneath the house-hunting there may be a longing for a family that's more honest with each other.

With a parent, a conversation about the past could open up, and you may be rehearsing how it'll go. With the house itself, you might be browsing places you can't afford or planning a renovation in your head. With the people you live with, there may be a wish for more closeness that nobody's said out loud. Make one room as good as you can with what you've already got.
4.reversed:
Home can become somewhere you imagine better than you live in, when this card is reversed in the fourth. The dream house, the ideal family, and meanwhile the dishes and the difficult conversation both pile up. Water on water with nothing to stop it can make nostalgia heavy, and you might spend evenings in old photos. The fourth is angular, so this doesn't stay private for long.

With family it can show as an idealised memory of a parent that stops you seeing them as they are. At home it's clutter, and projects half finished. With housemates or a partner, you might withdraw into your own room and your own head. Clear one corner of the house you've been avoiding, and keep it clear.

5.upright:
Venus has its joy in the fifth house, which means it does its best work here, in romance, play, creativity, children and whatever simply delights you. So this card in the fifth brings plenty of romantic and creative options and a lot of pleasure in imagining them. It's a card in a house it likes.

The complication is that the house's natural sign is Leo, and Scorpio squares Leo, with fire and water opposed on top of that. The fifth wants open, sunny delight, and the card brings Scorpio's intensity and secrecy into it. That's friction, and friction forces some kind of move. A light flirtation can get serious fast. A hobby turns into an obsession. Creatively you may have several ideas at once, all of them rich and none of them finished, and in romance the other person may be partly someone you've imagined.

In love, notice whether you're falling for the person or for the story you've built around them. With a creative project, you might have four on the go and have finished none. With children, if you have them, you might be dreaming big on their behalf, and it's worth asking what they'd pick. Give one creative thing a regular hour that nothing else is allowed to take.
5.reversed:
In the fifth house, the card reversed can mean play that's lost its fun. A romance lives mostly in messages and imagining. A creative idea stays in the notebook because making it real might spoil it. The square between Scorpio and Leo turns delight into brooding, and Venus, which ought to enjoy itself here, sits about waiting for the perfect conditions.

In dating it shows as chasing someone who isn't available, or keeping someone keen without meeting them. With hobbies, it's buying the equipment and leaving it in the box. Pleasure starts to feel like something you'll get round to. With children, worrying about their future might be taking the place of enjoying them. Pick one small pleasure and do it badly, for fun, without deciding what it means.

6.upright:
The sixth house is the actual daily routine. The job you do each day, the chores, the meals, the sleep, the body's upkeep. Its natural sign is Virgo, where Venus is in fall, so the card's way of working rubs against what this house wants. Venus is about pleasure, and the sixth is about getting through the list.

There's help, though. Scorpio makes a sextile to Virgo, a cooperative angle that needs taking up, and earth and water are friendly. So in the sixth this card tends to show as daydreaming about a different routine, a new diet, a new job, a four-day week, the morning ritual someone described online. Some of these are good ideas. The difficulty is that the sixth house works by repetition, and this card loves a plan far better than the fifth day of doing it. Mars has its joy here, and Mars likes effort.

At work you may be imagining a better job while the current one piles up on the desk. In the body, you could be trying lots of different routines and giving none of them long enough. With food there may be a pull toward a quick fix. Choose one small habit and keep it going for six weeks before you judge it.
6.reversed:
Routine slides while you plan a better one, when the card is reversed in the sixth. Meals get skipped, the list gets longer, the body gets tired, and you're reading about the perfect morning. Colleagues may notice you're a bit elsewhere. Venus in fall in Virgo's house finds it hard to enjoy anything ordinary, and upside down it stops trying.

At work, dull tasks may be piling up while you think about the job you'd prefer to have. With health, it can be chasing a promised fix in place of the plain basics. Sleep can go irregular too. Your space at home may be sliding as well, laundry, dishes, post. Do the dullest job on your list before anything else, and keep doing that for a while.

7.upright:
The person opposite you lives in the seventh house, a partner, a business partner, a contract, even a rival you deal with face to face. Libra is its natural sign and Venus its natural ruler, so the card's planet is on home ground here. Drawn here, this card puts relationships at centre stage, and there may be more than one possibility on the table.

Scorpio sits right next to Libra, a semi-sextile, neighbours with little in common, and water and air are neutral to each other. So Libra's fair, even partnership meets Scorpio's deep and possessive way of wanting, with Venus in detriment in the card's sign. You may catch yourself imagining a partner who's everything, passionate and fair and loyal and always there. You may be comparing the person you've got with people you've only pictured. If you're single, there could be several people in view and none of them actually chosen.

In a relationship, notice whether you're seeing your partner or your picture of them. In business, a partnership or contract might look ideal, so read it twice and ask someone else to read it too. With a rival, you might be imagining their life as much better than it is. Have one honest conversation with your partner about what each of you actually wants from the next few years.
7.reversed:
A relationship run on fantasy is the risk with the card reversed in the seventh. You might be waiting for someone to turn into the person you imagined, or holding onto a partnership because of what it was supposed to become. Venus rules this house and is in detriment in the card's sign, so your read on people gets clouded.

In business it can be a partner who promised a great deal and delivered little, and you keep giving them one more chance. In love it might be an ex you still idealise, which makes whoever's actually there look dull. Contracts signed in a hurry are worth a second look. Write down three things your partner actually does for you, and let those count.

8.upright:
Intimacy, shared money, debts, inheritance and endings, these belong to the eighth house, Scorpio's natural house. The card's sign is Scorpio too, which makes this its own territory. It's water on water, and the amplification is strong. If any house knows what this card is about, it's this one.

What makes it complicated is Venus, which is in detriment in Scorpio, and that friction is part of the reading. Venus wants pleasure and ease, and the eighth deals in trust, sex, money that isn't only yours, and the fear of losing things. So the card's longing goes deep here and gets tangled. You might be imagining a closeness with someone that's intense and a bit frightening. You might be picturing how a joint account, a loan or an inheritance would work out if it went a certain way. Some of the cups in this house are about control. Some are about finally letting go of something you've held a long time.

In a relationship there may be a wish for more intimacy and a fear of asking for it. With shared money, a partner's spending or a family estate may be stirring up both fantasies and worries. With an ending, you might be picturing a very different outcome from the one that's likely. Sit down with the other person and look at one shared money matter in plain numbers.
8.reversed:
Intimacy can turn into a guessing game with this card reversed in the eighth. You imagine what the other person thinks, wants or is hiding, and act on the fantasy. The eighth is a house where things are meant to be shared, and the card has you keeping half of it back. With shared money it can mean avoiding the numbers altogether. The same-element pairing keeps everything intense, and with Venus uncomfortable in Scorpio, trust comes harder than usual.

It shows up as jealousy, secrecy, or a debt nobody's discussing. With an ending, you might keep the door half open because the fantasy of what could have been is easier to hold than the loss. In a close relationship, physical closeness may drop off while the imagining goes up. Ask the question you've been imagining the answer to.

9.upright:
Belief, study, travel and the long view make up the ninth house. The Sun has its joy here, and the natural sign is Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter. Drawn here, the card fills the horizon with options, places to go, courses to take, ideas and teachers that might explain everything.

Scorpio sits just before Sagittarius, a semi-sextile, and water and fire are opposed, so there's some steam in this. The card's intense, private longing comes into a house that wants openness and room to roam. You may find yourself drawn to a belief or a teacher promising deep answers, or planning a trip that's partly about getting away from something. Some of these cups are genuine and would widen your life. Some would be expensive detours. Telling them apart is harder than usual, because the longing makes everything look meaningful.

In study it can be several courses saved and none begun. With travel, a trip planned in detail and never booked, or booked on a feeling. In belief, a new idea may feel like the answer to a question you've had for years. With in-laws or people from another culture, you might be romanticising a way of life you've only seen from outside. Learn one thing properly before you start collecting the next.
9.reversed:
Faith placed in the wrong thing is the usual story with this card reversed in the ninth. A course, a belief, a guru, a trip that promised to change everything and didn't. Fire and water clash in this house, and turned over, the card lets the steam fog your judgement about what's worth believing. The semi-sextile means the Scorpio longing and the Sagittarian search don't really understand each other.

It shows as money spent on programmes that deliver less than the brochure. It can be a move abroad that looked like a new life and felt like the old one with worse weather. Your views might harden, too, defended loudly because doubting them would hurt. Check the credentials of any teacher before you hand them your trust or your money.

10.upright:
Career, public role and reputation sit in the tenth house, the visible top of the chart. It's angular, so whatever happens here tends to be seen by a lot of people. Its natural sign is Capricorn, ruled by Saturn, and with this card here there are several career paths in front of you at once.

Scorpio makes a sextile to Capricorn, a cooperative angle, and earth and water feed each other, so something real can come of this with effort. The card's longing in the tenth tends to be about how you'd like to be seen. A title, a different profession, being recognised by the people who matter to you. The danger is choosing for image. You may picture yourself in several roles and like how each of them sounds when you say it at a party. Saturn, the house's natural ruler, is slow to reward anything that hasn't been tested.

At work, you may be tempted by an offer that sounds impressive and turns out ordinary. With a boss, there may be a gap between what you want and what you've told them. With your reputation, you could be guessing at how others see you and getting it wrong in both directions. Talk to someone who does the job you daydream about and ask them what an ordinary day looks like.
10.reversed:
Ambitions that stay in your head, that's the tenth house with the card upside down. You talk about the career you'd like and do very little toward it. Or you chase a role for its prestige and find it hollow once you're in it. The sextile to Capricorn is an opening that has to be used, and reversed, it isn't.

It shows as a CV rewritten many times and rarely sent, or a job taken for the title. With a parent, there may be old expectations about what you'd become. At work, a colleague may be doing the thing you keep talking about. Write down what you'd like a normal working day to feel like, and check your plans against that.

11.upright:
Friends, networks, groups and hopes for the future all belong to the eleventh house. Jupiter has its joy here, and the natural sign is Aquarius, ruled by Saturn and, in modern terms, Uranus. Here the card fills your social life and your hopes with options, groups to join, people to meet, futures to picture.

Scorpio squares Aquarius, two fixed signs, friction that forces some kind of move. Air and water have nothing against each other and nothing much in common either. So the card's deep, personal longing comes into a house of groups and shared ideals, and it doesn't always fit. You may want a closeness from a friendship that a group can't give. You may be picturing a future with several different sets of people and not sure which one is yours. There can be a pull toward the exclusive circle, the inner group, the people who seem to be having a better time.

With friends, you might be idealising someone new and overlooking an old friend who's been steady for years. In a club, a network or an online group, you could be drawn into a scheme that sounds good because everyone's excited. With your hopes, there may be several futures and no plan. Tell a friend about one hope in enough detail that it starts to become a plan.
11.reversed:
Hopes that stay vague and friendships that never quite deepen, those are the eleventh house with the card reversed. You may join groups and drift away before anyone knows you. The square with Scorpio creates tension between wanting to belong and not trusting anyone enough to try. Both signs are fixed, and neither gives way easily.

It shows in a friend you never quite trust, or a plan with others that never gets off the ground. Online, it can be watching a group's life from outside and imagining it's better than yours. Some of your hopes might belong to people you used to be close to. A cause you once cared about may have gone quiet in you. Ring one friend and make a real plan, with a date and a place.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the hidden side of life, retreat, sleep, dreams, what goes on behind closed doors and below the surface of the day. Its natural sign is Pisces, where Venus is exalted, so the card is welcomed here, and Scorpio makes a trine to Pisces. If there's a house where this card is most at home, it's this one.

Dreams run vivid. Imagination runs rich. Scorpio and Pisces are both water, and the same element in the card and the house turns the volume up, the good and the too much alike. You may find yourself spending a lot of time in your own head, daydreaming, remembering, rehearsing. Some of it is restoring you. Some of it is escape, and it can be hard to tell which from the inside. Saturn has its joy in this house, which is a reminder that solitude works best with some structure to it.

Sleep may bring long, memorable dreams, and you may need more of it than usual. In private, you might want more time alone, and it's worth taking. With creative work, the ideas may come from somewhere you can't explain, and they're worth catching. Keep a notebook by the bed and write down what you dream before you check your phone.
12.reversed:
Escape that has gone on too long is what this card reversed can mean in the twelfth. Sleep, screens and daydreams take up more of the day, and you withdraw from people without quite deciding to. Venus is exalted in Pisces and loves the dream too much to want to wake up. Water on water with nothing to hold it back makes the retreat very comfortable, and very hard to come out of.

It shows as isolation, secrecy, or a habit you keep private because you know it's not helping. Friends may feel you've disappeared. At work you could be there in body and miles off in your head. Spend regular time with someone who grounds you, and tell them one thing you've been keeping to yourself.
